# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if any code path returns an error the
model does not sanction.

| `PF-04` | `build` | A file under a source root is not a profile file: the profile file set drops it, and for every other file list, review list and toolchain the profile ID with that file equals the profile ID without it. |
| `PF-05` | `build` | The order of the rows does not change the profile ID: four reorderings of the four profile files, one of them with a source file added, give the ID of the original order, and a repeated path is refused with DuplicatePath. |
| `PF-06` | `build` | A profile has one language: a package of the profile's language is admitted and a package of another language is refused with LLC0103, for each of the nine pairs of the languages 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 that the owner values admit; the first refusal of a package list is the answer, and the code is the one the pinned LexLean returns for a lexicon whose language does not match the project's. |
| `PF-07` | `some-true` | The Atlas lexicon lexlean.uor.atlas@1.0.0 of the pinned LexLean is language 1.0 and holds 293 entry files with distinct ids, each a document denotation into the module Atlas, and the project examples/uor-atlas holds 86 source modules, all core modules, 80 at the top and 6 under Prelude, that include the module Atlas; the model's package, version, language, counts, entry ids and module names equal that copy. |
| `PF-08` | `build` | An Atlas profile serves all 293 entries: every entry denotes the module Atlas, the module Atlas is among the 86 modules of the profile, and the number of served entries is 293; without the module Atlas no entry is served, an entry into a module the profile lacks is not served, and the owner values give the uor-atlas profile the language 1.0, so a package of language 1.2 is refused with LLC0103. |
| `PF-09` | `build` | Each law of the profile model rejects its planted defect: a root that matches a prefix instead of a whole component, a profile file set that keeps source files, a serve check that counts an entry into a missing module and a language rule that admits another language each fail lexlean verify; PROFILES.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |

## store

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ST-01` | `build` | The store layout of lexlean-mcp/store/1 is a closed type of seven directories, profiles, drafts, builds, verifications, index, exports and keys, in that order: each has one distinct wire name, every directory is listed, every wire name parses back to its directory and an unknown name is refused. |
| `ST-02` | `build` | The backup set is exactly verifications, keys and the drafts references: the predicate is membership of that set, every item that cannot be recomputed and does not expire is in it, nothing recomputable is in it, and the archive has exactly those three fields. |
| `ST-03` | `build` | Retention is a total function of the bound owner values: an attestation record never expires at any age, a draft record expires after store.draft_retention (30 days) and not before, and both durations are the values bound in src/OwnerValues.lex.tex. |
| `ST-04` | `build` | The drift check is a total function from the stored profile record, the lock check result, the recomputed profile ID and the recomputed toolchain hashes to one of NoDrift, LockDrift, IdDrift and ToolchainDrift, deciding in that order of precedence: lock, then ID, then toolchain; all eight inputs of the decision are tabulated, and a recomputation that Identity refuses is IdDrift. |
| `ST-05` | `build` | The lifecycle is a state machine over the served revision, the served profile set, the previous release, the retired profiles and the records: rollout, rollback, upgrade and retirement keep every record, rollback restores the previous revision and served set, an upgrade serves the new profile and a retired profile is not served. |
| `ST-06` | `build` | AC-14 (model): the profile preimage determines its toolchain field for every input, so a new LexLean revision gives another preimage, and after an upgrade the earlier records still resolve and still validate; this is a claim about preimages, not about SHA-256. |
| `ST-07` | `build` | AC-15 and AC-17 (model): returning to the previous revision serves its profiles and its revision, a record written after the rollout still resolves after the rollback, and a release rollback resolves every record that resolved before it. |
| `ST-08` | `build` | AC-16 (model): after restore from a backup every backed-up record resolves as before, the keys and the draft references are restored, and re-verifying a restored record yields the attestation ID it is stored under because the ID is a function of the profile and the inputs; the signed attestation format stays abstract until #11. |
| `ST-09` | `build` | Each law of the store model rejects its planted defect: an attestation that expires, a drift check that reports ToolchainDrift before IdDrift, a rollback that drops a later record and a restore that omits keys each fail lexlean verify; STORE.md records the command, the diagnostic and the restore of each. |

| `TL-01` | `build` | The tools of F4 to F7 declare one schema each: lexlean_check, lexlean_snapshot, lexlean_format and lexlean_build take project (a non-empty string), files (strings) and all (a boolean), lexlean_format also check_only, and no other member; each declares an outputSchema, the lexlean/command-result/1 object for check, format and build and an object with a spec for snapshot; tools/list through the production core shows exactly these, and a call whose arguments break the schema is refused by the core as an Invalid arguments error result before any effect is asked for, while a call the schema admits and the tool cannot make (all together with files, a file name with a line feed) is the protocol error invalid params, and neither is ever an answer of the Engine. |
| `TL-02` | `build` | An answer of the Engine is a tool result and never a protocol error: class 0 gives a result without isError whose structuredContent is the canonical command result, classes 1, 2 and 4 give isError true with the command result of the failure, the text block is the same JSON, a host failure (project-refused, engine-unavailable) gives isError true with its failure name, and bytes that are not a command result or whose exit_code differs from the class are a typed internal refusal of the core. |

| `TL-05` | `build` | lexlean_format agrees with lexlean fmt: on the same fixtures check_only true gives the result of lexlean fmt --check and writes nothing, and check_only false gives the result of lexlean fmt and leaves the project with the same files, byte for byte. |
